newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate falls to 13.174 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate falls to 13.174 pct.

text.p: The Philippine 91-day treasury bill yield fell to 13.174 pct from 13.217 last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The 182-day T-bill fell to 13.756 percent from 14.018.
The 364-day T-bill fell to 13.106 percent from 14.228.
The Treasury had earlier said it would offer bills totally worth 2.5 billion pesos but at the auction it accepted tenders worth 2.7 billion.
The Treasury said the extra 200 million pesos were on tenders for the one-year bills.
For the first time this year, the T-bills auction has produced an inverted yield curve with the one-year yield lower than the three and six months.
"We were pleasantly surprised that the 364-day went down by 112 basis points. That's why we accepted more," National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said.
Out of offers of 4.105 billion pesos for the one-year bills, the Treasury accepted 700 million.
It accepted one billion pesos from offers of 2.52 billion for the six-months bills and one billion pesos from offers of 1.405 billion for the three-months bills.
